{{Short description|Type of family as defined by the United States Census Bureau}}

A '''family''' is defined by the [[United States Census Bureau]] for statistical purposes as "a group of two people or more (one of whom is the [[household|householder]]) related by birth, marriage, or adoption, and residing together; all such people (including related subfamily members) are considered as members of one family."

A '''family household''' is more inclusive, consisting of "a household maintained by a householder who is in a family (as defined above), and includes any unrelated people (unrelated subfamily members and/or secondary individuals) who may be residing there."<ref>US Census Bureau</ref>

In 2014, the US Census Bureau began including [[same-sex marriages]] in their counts of families and family households. Prior to this, they were counted as [[cohabitation|cohabiting partners]]; thus, they were not considered as forming a family.<ref>Cohn</ref>
